    - Edgar Penhallow, of the Cordwainers' Guild in Selsior, at your service. Visiting for the season. To study the workshops. And report back. At the end of summer. Yes.
    - *Player*! Notebook five is filling nicely. I have written down 'simple always wins' and 'a boot should outlive its owner' on facing pages. They argue with each other when I close the book. I can almost hear them.
    - *Player*. The letter went off with the carter, all about soles and welts. My mother will be very pleased. The other sheet is still in notebook five. Folded small. It is quite safe there.
    - How may I help you? Please, do ask anything.
        - *Choice:* What's in your notebooks?
        - *Choice:* How do you find Urbanograd?
        - *Choice:* What about Cobble?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thank you.
    - One is measurements: every boot last on the Row. Two is all drawings of Rivet's lift; Rivet lets me hold the tools, which in Selsior would take four years and a fee. Three is everything else: Dyna's colours, Jinx's juggling, and a page of notes from the Open Table headed 'Who is in charge?'
    - The answer, I am now fairly sure, is 'everyone, loudly'. Four is boots. Only boots. Five I began last week. I am not yet sure what it is about.
    - Loud. Bright. Nobody asks to see my guild papers. On my first day I said please to a door, and Jinx laughed so hard that all five apples came down at once. I was mortified. Now I say please to every door on purpose. Rivet says that is my first act of rebellion.
    - Master Cobble invented the soft-soled rooftop boot by himself, without a guild, without a single form. I have asked him three times to take me on. He said I have the wrong sort of hands. I sweep his step every morning anyway. The step does not mind my hands.
    - I believe Master Cobble kept the sheath on the awl. I saw it by his bench yesterday. He did not mention it. I did not mention it. We are both being terribly polite about it. I think it is the best conversation we have ever had.
    - Thank you so much. Please, after you. No, truly, after you.
